key: e:mine health and safety regulations 8.10.1.2 b
synopsis: South African regulation 8.10.1.2(b) covers underground trackless mobile machines against pedestrians; its companion 8.10.2.1(b) covers machine-to-machine collisions where significant collision risk exists, and both commenced on 21 December 2022 through Gazette No. 47790, Notice 2908 [f2273]. The skeptic’s review reports that these provisions had been suspended in 2015 because the technology was unavailable [f10724]. Their requirements combine automatic detection and effective warning with slowing a diesel-powered trackless mobile machine to a safe speed and automatically applying its brakes when no preventive action is taken; the system must also fail to safe without human intervention [f2274, f2275, f2276, f10723]. Together with MOSH performance requirements and verification, these are existing off-road provisions [f1713]. The corpus highlights a difference in emphasis: South Africa legally mandates Level 9 intervention, whereas NSW and NIOSH bowtie work favor Levels 1–6 controls such as segregation and site design, treating Levels 7–9 collision systems as backup [f3624].

relations.note: Adds the 2015 suspension and technology-unavailability explanation to the commencement history.
Both identify 21 December 2022 as the regulatory milestone.
Specifies diesel machines, safe speed, and braking when no preventive action is taken.
Both require fail-to-safe operation without human intervention.
Adds automatic detection and effective warning to the intervention requirements.
Automatic braking without human intervention substantiates the legally mandated Level 9 characterization.
Documented commencement supports classification as existing off-road provisions.
Defines the collision scenarios covered by the summarized braking and fail-safe duties.
